featured_reviews.name: Sanika Ghag
featured_reviews.review_text:
NO, JUST A BIG FAT NO.

I recently visited Aditi Hospital for a MINOR surgery as recommended to me by Dr. Shrirang Yadwadkar (my surgeon). While I have nothing but good words and gratitude for Dr. Shrirang, the staff, the resident doctors and the overall administration at Aditi Hospital made my entire experience quite abysmal and displeasing.

The state of rooms post my operation was beyond terrible. The bed had weird stains and marks, the bed cover had stains, the bedsheets was that old state of white that happens after one too many washes and was smelling horrible, the bed and pillow was hard as a rock, the washroom had wires running through it and the structure in general looked like it would fall any minute - all this after paying for a PRIVATE ROOM (check attached photos).

But I think the real nail in the coffin was their hospitality, absolutely unhinged. We were given a room close to the nurses station, and it was noisy as hell. It was only me and my mom sleeping in the room and their staff - both male and female, would come in and out at of our room at their will, without knocking or without waiting for our approval. The administration staff is also not well versed with the mediclaim policies.

The worse is yet to come. 1 and 1/2 hour after my anaesthesia came off, a resident doctor came in to take my vitals then actually has handed me my phone and asked me to write a review - my operation was done on my right hand... No doctor, sister, nurse, anyone actually even asked once how my health was, just came in took my vitals and went. We were supposed to get discharged by 5 but the doctors kept us waiting citing that the OT summary wasn't provided by the surgeon so the discharge note could not be made. We told them to call the surgeon and ask for it and for 2 hours they didn't do so and kept us hanging. Finally, taking matters into my own hands, I had to call the surgeon myself and ask him to send the required data to the hospital staff. Even after this, no one has come in to explain me anything about my post-op care, diet, health precautions, etc.

Furthermore, when my mom went to ask about my post-op care, one nurse told her to visit the doc downstairs. Like, where is your hospitality? Asking a patient's family member to hunt for doctor's in your hospital and not actually taking the time to come and talk to your own patients?

Pissed at this treatment, I had to go and talk to their doctor who still had a very oh-I-don't-care about this attitude and was quite rude. I thought the day was past me, but upon reaching home I realised the doctors had left 2 ECG monitors still strapped on my chest - 12 hours post surgery.

If I could give a no star review to this hospital, I very well would.  If you are looking for patient care, hospitality, quiet and peaceful time at the hospital where you or your loved ones could blissfully recover, ADITI HOSPITAL IS NOT IT.

featured_reviews.name: anita verma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review to share a very horrible experience I had at this hospital on 1st January 2025, during my mother’s treatment.

In the last week of December 2024, my mother was diagnosed with a serious issue related to her gall bladder, and she underwent surgery here. On 1st January, when I visited her room, the doctor came for dressing change and asked me to step outside for a few minutes. Since it was just for a short time, I left my purse in the room.

After the doctor left, a cleaning staff member entered the room and locked the door from inside. I was standing outside waiting, but the door did not open for several minutes. When I asked the nurse about it, she said the dressing was already done. I questioned why the door was locked, and when the nurse knocked, the cleaning staff suddenly rushed out, looking very nervous.

When I entered the room, my mother immediately told me to check my purse. On checking, I found that more than ₹3,000 cash was missing.

We immediately informed the hospital staff, but initially no action was taken. Only after my elder sister strongly complained did the staff start responding. CCTV footage was checked, but unfortunately, there was no camera inside the room. However, the footage outside clearly showed suspicious behavior of the staff member. Even her purse was checked, but we were told nothing was found. Later, instead of strict action, the staff member was simply shifted to another duty.

This incident deeply affected us. My mother had just undergone surgery costing nearly ₹2 lakhs, and instead of feeling safe, she was in tears thinking that theft was happening inside a hospital room.

Hospitals are places where patients and families should feel secure. This experience broke our trust completely. I am posting this review now because I finally have the time and emotional strength to speak about it.

I hope the hospital management takes serious responsibility, improves security, CCTV coverage, and ensures that no other family has to face such trauma again.

I hope this review helps others stay alert and take extra care of their personal belongings while focusing on their loved ones’ recovery.

featured_reviews.name: Anand N
featured_reviews.review_text:
A family member spent many days in the ICU at Galaxy Superspeciality Hospital, Mulund East, following a surgery performed at the same hospital. To be fair, the surgery was successful and we have no complaints regarding the doctors and nursing staff who treated the patient. Unfortunately, our overall experience with the hospital's management and facilities was extremely disappointing.

The biggest concern was hygiene and cleanliness. We observed cockroaches in the reception area on multiple occasions almost everyday. The reception floor would often remain dirty with shoeprints and smudges for hours without being cleaned. There was also a pile of garbage near the hospital entrance that frequently produced an unpleasant smell.

Another major issue was the complete lack of proper washroom facilities for visitors and attendants. It is difficult to understand how a multi-speciality hospital can operate without providing basic restroom facilities for families of admitted patients. Female members of our family were often forced to use a small and poorly maintained staff washroom.

The behavior and professionalism of some non-medical staff was also concerning. We observed staff members speaking loudly amongst themselves in the reception area and, on multiple occasions, playing videos on their mobile phones at an audible volume. We were also concerned by what appeared to be a reception staff member who seemed semi-intoxicated on several occasions. Seeing such behavior at the front desk of a hospital raises serious questions about management oversight.

The reception area itself has no air conditioning. Families of ICU patients are often required to spend long hours waiting for updates, and sitting for hours in Mumbai's heat with only old fans for ventilation made an already difficult situation even more uncomfortable.

We also experienced a critical administrative error where a prescription handed to us contained both the wrong surname and wrong age for our patient. We had to verify with two different members of the hospital staff that we were purchasing the correct medicines. Such mistakes should never occur in a professional healthcare setting.

While we appreciate the care provided by the doctors and nurses, the hospital's poor hygiene standards, inadequate facilities, administrative lapses, and lack of professionalism among some support staff left us with a very negative impression and multiplied our emotional distress levels.

My dad was taken to Manisha Universal Hospital at night. When we reached the upper gate of the hospital, it was locked, and the staff couldn’t find the key. There was no one at the reception. We knocked on the door, but there was no response for about 5 minutes. Then one person came and said they couldn’t find the key. It took them 20 minutes to finally get it.Unfortunately, in those 20 minutes, my dad suffered a heart attack right outside the hospital. After that, he was immediately taken to the ICU due to severe chest pain. His treatment started, and the next day the doctors told us that an angiography needed to be done. We gave our consent for it.There was an operation theatre in the hospital itself, but without properly informing us, they decided to shift him to another hospital. They didn’t take permission from any family member. An ambulance was called, and they suddenly took him away. When we asked where they were taking him, they replied, "We don’t know."One of our relatives went along in the ambulance, and the rest of us followed. He was taken to **Galaxy Hospital in Mulund East** and admitted to the ICU there. The hospital staff told us that the doctor (Dr. Dhamandeep) would arrive in 15 minutes, but he came only after 1.5 hours.My dad was then taken into the operation theatre for the angiography. When the reports came, we were informed. However, during the process, the hospital staff misbehaved with us. The family members who were present with the patient were treated very rudely. The staff kept pushing us and telling us to go downstairs, that we were not allowed to stay there — even though we explained that our patient was in a serious condition.
After the angiography, an ambulance was called again, and my dad was shifted back to **Manisha Hospital.The patient had mediclaim insurance, but the hospital staff just wanted money, which is why the doctor kept delaying the operation. The doctor had said that the surgery would be done on Saturday afternoon. But then he left the hospital. Later, when the patient’s wife went to the reception to ask what time the surgery was scheduled, they said there was no surgery planned.
At that moment, another doctor told the patient in the ICU that the operation would happen on Monday. When we called Dr. Sagar, he said the operation won’t happen until an application number is generated. So we asked him why he had been saying for the last 3 to 4 days that the operation would be done. Suddenly, he changed his statement and said that the patient’s wife and daughter had refused the operation — which was a complete lie.
Why would the family refuse the surgery when the patient’s condition was critical? Then he said we have to pay ₹20,000 for the operation, otherwise it won’t be done. It was clear that they just wanted money, which is why they kept the patient in the ICU for so long and gave us a bill of ₹1.66 lakhs. They wanted to keep the patient admitted longer to fully exhaust the mediclaim, which is why they delayed the surgery.
The medicine bill alone was ₹73,000 — but the patient said he was not even given that many medicines, especially since no treatment was given in the last 3 days. The doctors kept giving contradictory information — different stories each time. This hospital is a fraud.We stayed in that hospital for 5 days, and we saw 3 such similar cases. Once they get the money, they stop the treatment. So, everyone please be cautious — never go to this hospital for treatment. We have suffered a lot over the last 5 days
